video_title: A Conversation About Basketball, Science, and the Universe with Neil deGrasse Tyson

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: Neil deGrasse Tyson questions the fair pole rule in basketball
quotes.excerpt: Is basketball the only sport where, if your foot or the ball hits the line, it's out?
quotes.quote: Is basketball the only sport where, if your foot or the ball hits the line, it's out rather than in? What's the college football, college football's different with the foot. One foot, two foot. But a touchdown just has to touch the line. Even though the line is this wide, it just has to touch the line. For the ball, for sure. So American football is the only one like, but if your foot touches the line, you're running down, that's out. They should call it the fair pole. They should call it the fair pole.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: General relativity and quantum physics are fundamentally incompatible theories
quotes.excerpt: general relativity, the theory of the large, as you surely know, does not comport with quantum physics
quotes.quote: Right now, general relativity, the theory of the large, as you surely know, does not comport with quantum physics, the theory of the small. Quantum physics, space is quantized. That's where we get the quantum from, whereas in general relativity, space is continuous. You can't have, what? What? Okay, so the shotgun marriage occurred at the Big Bang when the large was small. And if the large was small, does quantum physics affect the entire universe if the whole universe is small? This is where we get a multiverse from, because you have quantum fluctuations and one of them pops out a whole new universe. If all universes are small, pop out a new one and it makes a new universe.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: The search for a unified field theory remains an elusive goal
quotes.excerpt: which Einstein searched for, gave up trying, people have been looking for for decades
quotes.quote: I'm just saying, one of three things: Maybe there is one we haven't found it yet. Maybe there isn't one at all. Maybe they are fundamentally incompatible, deal with it. Or, here's an even tougher pill: Maybe we're just too stupid. Maybe humans, why should the human brain be smart enough to deduce all this deducible in the universe? Is it even achievable? Is it supposed to be achievable? This is my point. We have accomplished more now to what felt unrealistic 100, 200, 300 years ago. However, people have been looking for a unified field theory of the universe, which Einstein searched for, gave up trying, people have been looking for for decades.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: Humans share 98% of their DNA with chimpanzees
quotes.excerpt: 98 plus percent identical DNA. What does the smartest chimp do?
quotes.quote: What's the closest genetic relative to humans? A primate of any kind. Monkey, chimpanzee. Chimpanzee. 98 plus percent identical DNA. What does the smartest chimp do? A smarter chimp can stack boxes to reach a banana. They have a few other things they do. A toddler could do that. And we have 98% identical DNA. So, if you're religious or you feel strongly about making sure we are distinct from the rest of the animal kingdom, you would say, what a difference that 1% makes.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing human intelligence to the James Webb Space Telescope
quotes.excerpt: Suppose the difference between stacking boxes to reach a banana and the James Webb Space Telescope
quotes.quote: Here's the thought experiment. Suppose the difference between stacking boxes to reach a banana and the James Webb Space Telescope, suppose that difference is as small as that 1% indicates. You say, come on, Tyson, no. Of course, there's a big difference. Suppose it isn't. Here's a way to think about it. Get some other species from another planet that is the same 1% in intelligence beyond us, in that same vector direction that we are beyond chimps. What would we look like to them? Chimps.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.excerpt: We can't meaningfully communicate with any other animal in the world
quotes.quote: It might be that they can't communicate with us because they cannot bring their brain to such a low level to make any sense to us at all. We can't meaningfully communicate with any other animal in the world. Their brains are bigger than ours. We can't meaningfully communicate with any other animal in the world.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: The complexity of human knowledge compared to basic skills
quotes.excerpt: You will never successfully teach it long division or the multiplication table
quotes.quote: No matter how smart your chimp is, we can probably agree you will never successfully teach it long division or the multiplication table. That's not calculus, that's not engineering, that's not building a bridge, the simplest thing. So what would these aliens be thinking of, casually in their day, that would transcend the greatest thoughts ever had by any human?

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: The solar system as a choreographed cosmic ballet
quotes.excerpt: The spinning planets orbit the sun along their appointed paths like pirouetting dancers
quotes.quote: The spinning planets orbit the sun along their appointed paths like pirouetting dancers in a cosmic ballet, choreographed by the forces of gravity. The universe is itself a dance.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: The sun and moon's unique size relationship
quotes.excerpt: The sun is 400 times bigger than the moon and 400 times farther away
quotes.quote: The sun is 400 times bigger than the moon and 400 times farther away. So they have the same size on the sky. And so that when the moon comes in front of the sun, you get a total solar eclipse, bucket list for anybody on Earth.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: Human vision is tuned for daytime activity
quotes.excerpt: We are awake and do our business in the daytime
quotes.quote: Because we are awake and do our business in the daytime. And that's so it's an evolutionary thing. Insects love twilight. They see very well ultraviolet because the sky is a very deep violet in when the sun is low on the horizon, and so that awakens them. And that's why it's evidence we're smarter than bugs, because bugs at appers are ultraviolet light and we attract them and zap them, they don't know any better.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mars' red color is due to iron oxide
quotes.excerpt: Mars is red from the color of the surface, it's basically rust, it's iron oxides in it
quotes.quote: Mars has an interesting element because Mars is red from the color of the surface, it's basically rust, it's iron oxides in it. And the there's very fine dust particles that get blown into the air. So that would make the daytime sky red. And given the optics of what's in the air, the setting sun because it's taking out all the red light, the setting sun would look blue. So it's the inverse of what we have here on Earth.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: Everything is a conspiracy when you don't know anything
quotes.excerpt: Everything is a conspiracy when you don't know anything about anything
quotes.quote: Everything is a conspiracy when you don't know anything about anything. Let's find out. Everything is a conspiracy when you don't know anything works.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.excerpt: I was eyewitness to September 11th, and I have my own camcorder footage of it
quotes.quote: I was eyewitness to September 11th, and I have my own camcorder footage of it. And there was conspiracy immediately rose up around it, that there were detonations put in the buildings, because it collapsed it like free fall was the claim. And so someone got my email, my email was a little more accessible back then, and said, you are eyewitness, tell me, how do you explain that it couldn't have been a plane if it free if it free fell? So I said, oh, let me go back to my camcorder, and I timed the fall. It took like three times longer. The whole thing happened quickly, but it took three times longer than it would have if it were in free fall. I calculated it using basic first week physics 101 equations. I wrote back to the guy, and I said, it was not in free fall. And he said, oh, you're part of the conspiracy.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: The tendency to view the world through conspiracy theories
quotes.excerpt: The less you know about the world, the more everything looks like a conspiracy to you
quotes.quote: The less you know about the world, the more everything looks like a conspiracy to you. You already claim you know what's true, and you make everything fit. And if there's a gap in the evidence for you, you say that's withheld, or that's in a conspiracy. The less you know about the world, the more everything looks like a conspiracy to you.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.summary_phrase: Stars manufacture the elements found on the periodic table
quotes.excerpt: Stars in their core manufacture elements, the elements we've come to know and love
quotes.quote: It's that stars in their core manufacture elements, the elements we've come to know and love on the periodic table. The universe wasn't born with those elements. The universe created them with heat and fusion, thermonuclear fusion. The stars that are best at that, they end their lives exploding, scattering that enrichment across the galaxy into gas clouds that enable the next generations of stars to have the ingredients of life, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, iron.

quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.excerpt: We are all made of stardust. We're part of a great unfolding cosmic story
quotes.quote: We are all made of stardust. We're part of a great unfolding cosmic story. We are a participant in that story. And because of that, not only are we alive in this universe, the universe is alive within us. And that is a 20th-century discovery of astrophysics that borders on the spiritual.
